title: Seven Killed in Attack on Church Funeral in Jordan's Karak; US Embassy Issues Alert
excerpt: Gunmen fired on a funeral at a Greek Orthodox church in Hammoud village, killing seven and injuring 27, as Jordan's king condemned a terrorist act and US citizens were told to expect heightened security nationwide.
body:
• Gunmen attacked a funeral at a Greek Orthodox church in Hammoud village, Karak Governorate, on October 23, killing seven people and injuring 27, Jordan's Public Security Directorate said.
  • The US Embassy in Amman issued a security alert: perpetrators are still being hunted, the area is cordoned off, and security has been increased at malls and other locations including foreign embassies in Amman.
  • King Abdullah II condemned the shooting as a terrorist act and vowed the harshest penalties; no group had claimed responsibility.
  • Indian nationals in Jordan should expect higher police presence nationwide, avoid areas of heavy police activity, and call 911 in an emergency.

Seven people were killed and 27 injured when gunmen opened fire during a funeral at a Greek Orthodox church in the village of Hammoud in Jordan's Karak Governorate on Friday, in an attack King Abdullah II condemned as terrorism and that prompted a US Embassy security alert for the whole country.

Jordan's Public Security Directorate (PSD) reported seven fatalities and 27 people undergoing treatment, figures carried in the US Embassy's alert and by The Hindu (Reuters), which said authorities described the attackers as extremists and that it was too early to determine links to groups inside or outside Jordan. Eyewitnesses told local media an explosion was heard as the funeral procession began, after which masked gunmen — one with a pistol, one with an AK-47 — fired for about five minutes at a congregation of more than 150 people inside and outside the church, according to NewsBytes, whose earlier report put the toll at six dead and 28 wounded before the PSD figures were issued.

"Some guys were standing outside the church before two people got out of a vehicle and started shooting. We were more than 150 people inside and outside the church."

— Tamer Halasa, eyewitness, to Al-Mamlaka TV

What the embassy advised

The US Embassy in Amman said security agencies were still hunting the perpetrators and had cordoned off the incident area. "There is also increased security at malls and other locations including foreign embassies in Amman. U.S. citizens should expect higher police presence in many parts of Jordan," the alert said. It advised citizens to enrol in the Smart Traveler Enrollment Program, avoid demonstrations, large gatherings and areas of heavy police presence, follow local authorities' instructions, and dial 911 in immediate danger. Jordan carries a US Travel Advisory Level 3: Reconsider Travel.

A governorate attacked before

Karak has been targeted before: in December 2016, Islamic State gunmen killed 10 people, including security officers and a Canadian tourist, in attacks centred on the governorate's Crusader-era castle. Christians number about 300,000 of Jordan's roughly 11.5 million people. King Abdullah II vowed authorities would "confront the terrorist act that targeted Karak with the harshest penalties," NewsBytes reported. No group had claimed responsibility as of Saturday.

What to watch

The manhunt for the two suspects is the immediate focus, along with whether churches across Jordan hold weekend services under the heightened security posture. Expatriates in Jordan — including its large Indian workforce — should follow PSD and embassy guidance, keep phones charged with emergency numbers saved, and avoid the Hammoud cordon area.
